source_text:
Ματθαῖος δὲ τὴν κατὰ ἄνθρωπον αὐτοῦ γένεσιν ἐξηγεῖται, βίβλος

γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ υἱοῦ Ἀβραάμ, καὶ πάλιν τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ γέννησις
οὕτως ἦν, ὅθεν καὶ ἀνθρωπόμορφον αὐτοῦ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ἐξεικονίζεται. Μάρκος δὲ
ἀπὸ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐξ ὕψους ἐπιόντος ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς τὴν ἀρχὴν
ἐποιήσατο, ἀρχὴν λέγων τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν τοῖς προφήταις· φωνὴ
βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, τὴν προφητικὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, διὰ τοῦτο δεικνὺς
καὶ τὴν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τοῦ λέοντος ἀνιστορίζων εἰκόνα· ἁγία τριὰς ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν σῶσον
ἡμᾶς τῇ χάριτί σου. Μάρκος ὁ εὐαγγελιστής, ἐπίσκοπος Ἀλεξανδρέων. Λουκᾶς ὁ
εὐαγγελιστής, οὗτοι οἱ δ' ἐκ τῶν οʹ τυγχάνουσιν διασκορπισθέντες ἐπὶ τῷ κηρύγματι
ᾧ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος· ἐὰν μή τις οὐ φάγῃ μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ πίῃ μου τὸ αἷμα, οὐκ ἔστι
131 μου ἄξιος. Ἀλλ' ὁ μὲν διὰ Πέτρου, ὁ δὲ διὰ Παύλου πάλιν ἐπανακάμψαντες πρὸς
κύριον εὐαγγελίσασθαι καταξιοῦνται ὑπὲρ οὗ καὶ ἐμαρτύρησαν, ὁ μὲν πυρποληθείς,
ὁ δὲ σταυρωθεὶς ἐπὶ ἐλαίας.
thought_title: Matthew and Mark symbols and the return of Mark and Luke
orientation: The author finishes linking Matthew to the man and Mark to the lion, then closes by naming Mark and Luke as men of the seventy who scattered and later returned.
pass_a_gloss: But Matthew expounds his birth according to man, saying Book of birth of Jesus Christ son of Abraham, and again But the birth of Jesus Christ was thus, for which reason also his gospel is depicted as formed like a man. And Mark made the beginning from the prophetic spirit coming from on high in the heavens, saying Beginning of the gospel, as it stands written in the prophets: Voice of one crying in the wilderness, showing the prophetic image of the gospel, for this reason also depicting the image of the lion in the wilderness. Holy Trinity our God save us by your grace. Mark the evangelist, bishop of the Alexandrians. Luke the evangelist, these four are from the seventy, having been scattered at the preaching which the Lord spoke: Unless anyone eats my flesh and drinks my blood, he is not worthy of me. But the one through Peter, the other through Paul, having turned back again to the Lord, are deemed worthy to preach the gospel, for the sake of which also they were martyred, the one having been burned with fire, the other having been crucified on an olive tree.

choices.english: his gospel is depicted as formed like a man
choices.why: keeps glossary man and gospel and avoids hyphenated compound while keeping passive depiction
rejected: his gospel is portrayed as anthropomorphic

choices.term: τὴν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τοῦ λέοντος ἀνιστορίζων εἰκόνα
choices.english: depicting the image of the lion in the wilderness
choices.why: ἀνιστορέω means depict or represent in a picture, not narrate, and the genitive links lion to image with wilderness as setting
rejected: narrating the lion in the wilderness
telling the image of the wilderness lion

choices.term: ἐὰν μή τις οὐ φάγῃ μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ πίῃ μου τὸ αἷμα, οὐκ ἔστι μου ἄξιος
choices.english: unless anyone eats my flesh and drinks my blood, he is not worthy of me
choices.why: μή with ἐάν plus οὐ before subjunctive is a double negative that yields unless eats, not unless does not eat
rejected: unless someone does not eat my flesh
if anyone does not eat my flesh

choices.term: ὁ μὲν πυρποληθείς, ὁ δὲ σταυρωθεὶς ἐπὶ ἐλαίας
choices.english: the one having been burned with fire, the other having been crucified on an olive tree
choices.why: keeps both aorist passive participles and ἐπί with genitive as place of crucifixion
rejected: the one burned, the other crucified on olive wood

bible_refs.note: βίβλος γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ υἱοῦ Ἀβραάμ
τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ γέννησις οὕτως ἦν
φάγῃ μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ πίῃ μου τὸ αἷμα

pass_b_english: Matthew recounts his human birth: “The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of Abraham” (Matthew 1:1), and again, “Now the birth of Jesus Christ took place in this way” (Matthew 1:18). For this reason his gospel is depicted as formed like a man.

Mark made his beginning from the prophetic Spirit coming down from on high in the heavens. He speaks of the beginning of the gospel (Mark 1:1), as it is written in the prophets: “A voice crying in the wilderness” (Mark 1:3). In this way he displays the prophetic character of the gospel and depicts the image of the lion in the wilderness. Holy Trinity, our God, save us by your grace.

Mark the evangelist was bishop of the Alexandrians, and Luke was the evangelist. These four, from the seventy, were among those who scattered at the preaching in which the Lord said, “Unless anyone eats my flesh and drinks my blood, he is not worthy of me” (cf. John 6:51–56, paraphrased). But the one returned to the Lord through Peter, and the other through Paul, and they were deemed worthy to preach the gospel. For his sake they were also martyred, the one burned with fire and the other crucified on an olive tree.
notes: 131 before μου ἄξιος is a stray page number, not source text
οὗτοι οἱ δ᾽ says four from the seventy but only Mark and Luke are named in this preserved clause

problems.quote: These men were among the seventy who scattered
problems.source_quote: οὗτοι οἱ δ' ἐκ τῶν οʹ τυγχάνουσιν διασκορπισθέντες
problems.why: Source specifies the four (evangelists) from the seventy; English drops δ' and reads like only Mark and Luke.
problems.fix: These four, from the seventy, were among those who scattered
problems.ruling: Source explicitly writes οὗτοι οἱ δ' ἐκ τῶν οʹ ("these four from the seventy"); English silently omits numeral δ' ("four"), altering the scope.

problems.quote: he is not worthy of me" (John 6:53)
problems.why: John 6:53 speaks of life in you, not being worthy; the tagged verse does not match the quoted words.
problems.fix: …he is not worthy of me" (cf. John 6:51–56, paraphrased).
problems.ruling: Source conflates John 6:53 with Matt 10:37–38 (οὐκ ἔστι μου ἄξιος); tagging only (John 6:53) misattributes "not worthy of me" to that verse.

problems.quote: For its sake they were also martyred
problems.source_quote: κύριον εὐαγγελίσασθαι καταξιοῦνται ὑπὲρ οὗ καὶ ἐμαρτύρησαν
problems.why: Because εὐαγγελίσασθαι is a verb, οὗ refers to κύριον (the Lord), not the gospel; they were martyred for him, not for it.
problems.fix: For his sake they were also martyred
problems.ruling: ὑπὲρ οὗ agrees with κύριον; martyrdom is for the Lord, not an unstated gospel neuter.

fixed: omission: fixed to 'These four, from the seventy' — source οὗτοι οἱ δ᾽ ἐκ τῶν οʹ specifies four
wrong_scripture: fixed citation to (cf. John 6:51–56, paraphrased) — source οὐκ ἔστι μου ἄξιος is not John 6:53 wording
